la:pron:ille.html:
ille (old orthog., olle), a, ud (ollus, a, um, Enn. ap. Müll.; ; in dramat. poets often ĭlle, v. Corss. Ausspr. II. p. 624),
gen. illī^us (usu. illĭus in epic and lyric poets; ; illīus in the time of Quint; cf. Ritschl, Opusc. 2, 683 sqq.; 696; gen. sing. m. illi, Cato ap. ; dat. sing. f. olli, ; and 154; abl. plur. † ab oloes = ab illis, Paul. ex Müll.); pron. demonstr. [Etym. dub., v. Corss. Beitr. p. 301], points (opp. hic) to something more remote, or which is regarded as more remote, and, in contrast with hic and iste, to something near or connected with a third person, that; he, she, it (absol.).
In gen.
With substantives: ille vir haud magna cum re sed plenus fidei, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 342 Vahl.): si quid vos per laborem recte feceritis, labor ille a vobis cito recedet ... nequiter factum illud apud vos semper manebit, Cato ap. : sol me ille admonuit,that sun,: in illa tranquillitate atque otio jucundissime vivere,: cum omnis arrogantia odiosa est, tum illa ingenii atque eloquentiae multo molestissima,: in illa vita,: illum Aurora nitentem Luciferum portet,.—
Absol.: illos bono genere gnatos, Cato ap. : ergo ille, cives qui id cogit, etc.,: tum ille, Non sum, inquit, nescius, etc.,; cf. ; : illum ab Alexandrea discessisse nemo nuntiat,; cf.: de illius Alexandrea discessu nihil adhuc rumoris,: ne illi sanguinem nostrum largiantur,.—In neutr. with gen.: Galba erat negligentior, quam conveniret principi electo atque illud aetatis,: illud horae,.—
With other pronouns: itaque cum primum audivi, ego ille ipse factus sum: scis quem dicam,; cf.: qui cum illis una ipsum illum Carneadem diligenter audierat,: ille quoque ipse confessus est,: huic illi legato,: hunc illum fatis Portendi generum,; cf.: hic est enim ille vultus semper idem quem, etc.,: hic est ille status quantitatis,: est idem ille tyrannus deterrimum genus,: eandem illam (sphaeram),: cum et idem qui consuerunt et idem illud alii desiderent,: illum reliquit alterum apud matrem domi,.—
Opp. to hic, to indicate that object which is the more remote, either as regards the position of the word denoting it, or as it is conceived of by the writer; v. hic, I. D.—
Pleon., referring back to a subject or object already mentioned in the same sentence: sic oculos, sic ille manus, sic ora ferebat,; cf. : non ille timidus perire, etc.,; : Parmenides, Xenophanes, minus bonis quamquam versibus, sed tamen illi versibus increpant, etc.,.
In partic.
Pregn., that, to indicate some well-known or celebrated object, equivalent to the ancient, the wellknown, the famous: si Antipater ille Sidonius, quem tu probe, Catule, meministi, : Xenophon, Socraticus ille,: auditor Panaetii illius,: a qua (gratia) te flecti non magis potuisse demonstras, quam Herculem Xenophontium illum a voluptate,: ut ex eodem Ponto Medea illa quondam profugisse dicitur,: magno illi Alexandro simillimus,: honestum illud Solonis est,: illa verba,: velocitas,.—
Particular phrases.
Hic ... ille, this ... that, the one ... the other, of single objects in opp. to the whole: non dicam illinc hoc signum ablatum esse et illud; hoc dico, nullum te Aspendi signum, Verres, reliquisse,.—
Ille aut or et ille, that or that, such and such: quaesisse, num ille aut ille defensurus esset,: commendo vobis illum et illum,.—
Ille quidem ... sed (autem, etc.), certainly, to be sure, indeed, etc., ... but still: philosophi quidam, minime mali illi quidem, sed, etc.,: ludo autem et joco uti illo quidem licet, sed, etc.,: Q. Mucius enucleate ille quidem et polite, ut solebat, nequaquam autem, etc.,: alter bellum comparat, non injustum ille quidem, suis tamen civibus exitiabile,: sequi illud quidem, verum, etc.,.—
Ex illo, from that time, since then (poet. and very rare): ex illo fluere et retro sublapsa referri Spes Danaūm, (for which in full: tempore jam ex illo casus mihi cognitus urbis Trojanae,): solis ex illo vivit in antris,: scilicet ex illo Junonia permanet ira,.— Hence, advv.
illā (sc. viā=ab hac parte), in that way, in that direction, there (very rare): nunc ego me illa per posticum ad congerrones conferam,; : hac vel illa cadit,: ac ne pervium illa Germanicis exercitibus foret, obsaepserat,; ; : ipsum quin etiam Oceanum illa tentavimus,: forte revertebar festis vestalibus illa, qua, etc., Merk. (vulg. illac).—
illō (sc. loco), to that place, thither (class.).
Lit., with verbs of motion, = illuc: principio ut illo advenimus, ubi primum terram tetigimus,: neque enim temere praeter mercatores illo adit quisquam,: nam illo non saxum, non materies advecta est,; ; : To. Vin' huc vocem? Do. Ego illo accessero, : positiones huc aut illo versae,.—
Transf.
To that end, thereto: haec omnia Caesar eodem illo pertinere arbitrabatur, ut, etc.,to that very purpose,: spectat,.—
Post-class. for ibi, there, .—
illim, adv., an early form (cf.: istim, exim) for illinc (i. e. illim-ce), from that place, thence (ante-class. and a few times in Cic.): sarculum hinc illo profectus illim redisti rutrum, Pompon. ap. (Fragm. Com. v. 90 Rib.); ; ; : illim equidem Gnaeum profectum puto, (al. illinc): quid illim afferatur,, b, 7 (al. illinc); : omnem se amorem abjecisse illim atque in hanc transfudisse,i. e. from her,; .

la:pron:illic.html:
illic (archaic ollic, acc. to Paul. ex Müll.), illaec, illuc, or illoc,
pron. [ille-ce].
He, she, or it yonder, that (only ante-class.): sed Amphitruonis illic est servos Sosia, A portu illic nunc cum laterna huc advenit,; : nimis demiror, Sosia, Qui illaec (i. e. Alcumena) illi me donatum esse aurea patera sciat,: cupio dare mercedem, qui illunc, ubi sit, commonstret mihi,: unde auscultare possis, quom ego illanc osculer,: latuit intus illic in illac hirnea,; cf.: quid illac impudente audacius?: sed quid illuc est?; cf. : illuc sis vide,: illuc est sapere?: cum illoc pacisce, si potes: perge obsecro: Pacisce quidvis, et saep.: ubi illic est scelus, qui me perdidit?that scoundrel,.—
With the interrogative part. ne: illicine, etc.: Si. Illicine est? Ps. Illic ipsus est, : illancine mulierem alere cum illa familia?.—
Hence, advv.
illac (sc. viā), that way, on that side, there: angiporto Illac per hortum circuit clam,: ita nunc hac an illac eam, incerta sum consili,: hac atque illac perfluo,: hac illac circumcursa,: omnes damnatos, omnes ignominia adfectos illac facere,stand on that side, belong to that party,.—
illuc or illoc (the old form, like hoc for huc), adv., to that place, thither.
Lit.
Form illuc: imus huc, illuc hinc; cum illuc ventum est, ire illinc lubet, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 258 Vahl.): clam illuc redeundum est mihi,: cum illuc veneris,: paulo momento huc illuc impelli, : huc illuc quasi vitabundi agitare,: salientes huc illuc,; so, huc atque illuc intuens,: huc et illuc Cursitant mixtae pueris puellae,: illuc ex his vinculis,i. e. into the other world,: proponimus illuc ire, ubi, etc.,: illuc, unde fugit mus,. —
Form illoc: post illoc veni quam, etc.,: cum illoc advenio, (dub.; Fleck. illo).—
Transf., to that person or thing, thereto (very rare): Pe. Illuc redi. Me. Quo redeam? Pe. Equidem ad phrygionem censeo, : quo res haec pertinet? illuc: Dum vitant stulti vitia, in contraria currunt,: illuc, unde abii, redeo: Nemon' ut avarus, etc.,; cf. : illuc cuncta vergere,to Nero,.—
To that point, to such a pitch: tunc adversis urgentibus, illuc decidit ut malum ferro summitteret,.

la:adv:illuc.gloss: thither, to that place, to there
senses: thither, to that place, to there

la:adj:illustris.html:
illustris (inl-), e (
nom. sing. masc. illuster. ; ), adj.
inlustro
, lighted up, clear, bright, light, lustrous (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. signif.).
Lit.: ostendebat Carthaginem de excelso et pleno stellarum, illustri et claro quodam loco, ; cf.: tum nec nimis illustres nec vehementer obscuros locos haberi oportet,: locus,: habitare bonis et illustribus domiciliis,: balnearia,: illustris et pellucida stella,: radii solis,: noctes,: caelum,.—Comp.: ostio et lumine illustriore,; cf.: solis candor illustrior est quam ullius ignis,: (ventus) tegulas illustriores fecit,.—
Trop.
Clear, plain, distinct, evident, manifest (syn. clarus): praeter haec, quae testata sunt et illustria, habeo multa occultiora,: his rationibus tam certis tamque illustribus, etc.,; cf.: illustribus igitur rebus insistis ... a certis et illustrioribus cohibes assensum,: nec vero ita disseram de re tam illustri tamque nota, ut, etc., Mos.: factum illustre notumque omnibus,: visus insignis et illustris,: illustris oratio est, si, etc. ... est enim haec pars orationis, quae rem constituat paene ante oculos ... est plus aliquanto illustre quam illud dilucidum: altero fit, ut intelligamus, altero vero ut videre videamur,: si desit illustris explanatio, propositio, etc.,: instruenda est vita exemplis illustribus,.—
Distinguished, respectable, famous, honorable, illustrious (cf.: clarus, insignis, spectabilis, nobilissimus, celeber, inclutus): homines illustres honore ac nomine,: illustrium hominum aetates et tempora persequi (shortly after: de clarorum virorum laudibus),: illustribus in personis temporibusque,: orator,: poëtae,: florens et illustris adulescens,: de antiquis illustrissimus quisque pastor erat,: philosophorum illustrissimi,: feminae,noble,; : cum illustribus provinciarum,: quorundam illustrium exsequiae,: paterfamiliae illustriore loco natus,: Themistoclis nomen est quam Solonis illustrius,: vitae ratio illustrior,; cf.: sunt illustriora quae publice fiunt,: haec vides quanto expressiora quantoque illustriora futura sint,: major atque illustrior res,more important, more remarkable,: causarum illustrium quascumque defendi nunc conficio orationes,.—Hence, adv. (acc. to II. A.), clearly, distinctly, perspicuously (very rare; only comp. and sup.): illustrius,; ; : illustrissime descripsit,.

la:verb:illustro.html:
illustro (inl-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
illustris
,
to light up, make light, illuminate (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. signif.).
Lit.: o, qua sol habitabiles Illustrat oras, maxime principum?: placida nocte leniter illustrante stellas,: ergastulum angustis illustratum fenestris, (but , read lustret).—
Trop. (acc. to illustris, II. A. and B.).
To make clear to the mind, to clear up, elucidate, illustrate, explain: ut ea consilia, quae clam essent inita contra salutem urbis, illustrarentur,; cf.: illustrantur, erumpunt omnia,; ; : omnia illustrata, patefacta, comperta sunt per me,; ; cf.: si modo id patefactum et illustratum est,; and: jus obscurum et ignotum patefacere et illustrare,: philosophiam veterem Latinis litteris illustrare,; cf. : illustrant eam (orationem) quasi stellae quaedam translata verba atque immutata,place in the right light, embellish, set off, adorn,; cf. : de illustranda oratione ut diceres,: orationem,; ; .—
To render famous, renowned, illustrious: aliquem laudibus, Luccei. ap. : quem Brutus cognomine suo illustravit,: familiam,: illustrabit, mihi crede, tuam amplitudinem hominum injuria,: humilius genus illustrasse factis, : summa quibus illustratur forum ingenia,; cf.: Padus poenā Phaëthontis illustratus,: vina maxime illustrata Messalae potu et salute,; ; cf.: quid prius illustrem satiris Musaque pedestri?; .

la:noun:ilium.gloss: the part of the abdomen extending from the lowest ribs to the pubes; the groin, flank
la:noun:ilium.html:
Īlĭum or Īlĭon, ĭi, n., = Ἴλιον,
a poetical name for Troja, the city of Ilium, Troy, ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—Called also īlĭos, i, f., acc. to the Gr. Ἴλιος, ; ; ; .—Also a later Ilium, built upon the coast, ; .—
Derivv.
īlĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Ilium, Ilian, Trojan: tellus,: res,: matres,: turmae,.—Subst.: īlĭi, ōrum, m., the Trojans, .—
īlĭăcus, a, um, adj., the same: orae,: classis,: fata,: Penates,: cineres,: amores,i. e. Paris,: hospes Didus,i. e. Æneas,: Vesta,worshipped at Troy,; hence, Alba, where also Vesta was worshipped,: carmen, i. e. Homer's Iliad, ; cf.: Macer,a poet who wrote on the Trojan war,: dextra,i. e. Ganymede's,: mons,i. e. Phrygian marble,: Iliacoque jugum memorabile remo,i. e. the promontory of Misenum, where Misenus, a follower of Æneas, was drowned,: muri, i. e. of Rome, as founded by descendants of the Trojan Æneas, ; hence, also, cuspis,of the consul Flaminius,.—Prov.: Iliacos intra muros peccatur et extra,.—
īlĭenses, ium, m., inhabitants of Ilium, Ilians, ; ; .—
īlĭădes, ae, m., the Trojan, i. e. Ganymede, .—
īlĭas, ădis, f.
The Trojan woman, i. e. Helen, .—In plur.: īlĭădes, um, Trojan women or girls, ; .—
The celebrated epic poem that describes the Trojan war, the Iliad, (3, 32), 66; . —On account of its great extent, used fig. to represent a great quantity or number, an Iliad, a whole Iliad, ; cf. written as Greek: tanta malorum impendet Ἰλιάς, ; and in plur.: tunc vero longas condimus Iliadas,.

la:adv:ilicet.html:
īlĭcet, adv.
i, root of īre, and licet; cf. scilicet and videlicet; lit., one may go; hence
,
In the oldest per. of the lang., a t. t. with which an assembly was dismissed when the business on hand was at an end, you may go; it is over: semper ilicet finem rei significat, ut actum est. Sic judices de concilio dimittebantur, suprema dicta cum praeco pronunciasset ilicet, quod significat ire licet, ; cf. ; ; so, at the end of funeral ceremonies, and 231.—
Transf.
(Ante-class. and rare.) Ilicet, let us go, let us be gone, : ilicet: Quid hic conterimus operam frustra?; : ilicet parasiticae arti maxumam malam crucem,the parasite's art may go and be hanged, Brix.—
All is over, to signify that any thing is lost or has failed (ante-class.): ilicet, mandata eri perierunt,; cf.: actum est, ilicet, me infelicem et scelestam,; , : ilicet, desine, jam conclamatum est,: ilicet, vadimonium ultro mihi facit,.—
Through the intermediate idea of hastening (cf.: ilico, extemplo; protinus, continuo, statim), straightway, immediately, instantly, forthwith (ante - class. and in

Aug. poets): an tu eloquens ilicet, Afran. ap. P.: fugit ilicet ocior Euro, Speluncamque petit,: ilicet ignis edax summa ad fastigia vento Volvitur,: ilicet obruimur numero,; (dub.; Müll. si licet); .

la:noun:ilex.html:
īlex, ĭcis, f.,

la:adv:illinc.html:
illinc, adv.
for illim-ce
,
from that place, thence.
Lit.: jube illos illinc abscedere,: illinc venire,: se illinc subducet,: illinc huc transferetur virgo,: illinc pallium mihi huc ferte,: illinc equidem Gnaeum profectum puto,: imperator utrimque hinc et illinc Jovi Vota suscipere,here and there,; cf.: et hinc et illinc,. —
Transf., from that person or thing, from that quarter, from or on that side: habeo pro meis, nec manu adseruntur; neque illinc partem quisquam postulat,: si illinc beneficium non sit, rectius putem quidvis domi perpeti,: illinc omnes praestigiae; illinc omnes fallaciae: omnia denique ab his mimorum argumenta nata sunt,; so opp. hinc: illinc cornicines, hinc praecedentia longi agminis officia,on one side ... on the other,.

la:verb:illabor.html:
illābor (inl-), psus, 3,
v. dep. n. [inlabor], to fall, slip, slide, glide, or flow into; to fall down, sink down (rare but class.).
Lit.: quo (i. e. in stomachum) primo illabuntur ea, quae accepta sunt ore,; : antennis illabitur ebria serpens,: notae jugis illabitur Aetnae,: si fractus illabatur orbis,should fall in, tumble to ruins,: tepet illabentibus astris Pontus,: rapidus fervor, per pingues unguine taedas illapsus,: conjugis illabi lacrimis, unique paratum scire rogum,to sink down dying,: qua Nar Tiberino illabitur amni,. —
Trop., to flow into, penetrate: si ea sola voluptas esset, quae quasi titillaret sensus, ut ita dicam, et ad eos cum suavitate afflueret et illaberetur,: sensim pernicies illapsa civium in animos,: da, pater, augurium, atque animis illabere nostris,enter into our minds,: animis illapsa voluptas,; with per, .

illūmĭnātio (inl-), ōnis, f.
illumino
,

la:verb:illumino.html:
illūmĭno (inl-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
in-lumino
,
to light up, make light, illuminate (class.; cf. illustro).
Lit.: luna illuminata a sole,: puteum (sole),: tabulata gallinarum parvis fenestellis,: vias igni,.—
Transf., to embellish or adorn with any thing bright: corona aurea fulgentibus gemmis illuminata,; : purpura omnem vestem illuminat,.—
Trop., to set in a clear light, to set off, make conspicuous (esp. freq. in rhetor. lang. of brilliant oratory): translatum, quod maxime tamquam stellis quibusdam notat et illuminat orationem,; cf. : orationem sententiis,: orationem translatorum nitore,: pulchritudinem rerum (claritas orationis),; : horum fidem Mitylenaeorum perfidia illuminavit,: nisi Thebas unum os Pindari illuminaret,made illustrious,: illuminata sapientia,.—Hence, * illūmĭnātē (inl-), adv., clearly, luminously: dicere,.

senses: to waste away, destroy something in sport; to violate, abuse, ruin
la:verb:illudo.html:
illūdo (inl-), si, sum, 3 (acc. to the first conj. illudiabant, ;
perf. subj. inlusseris, Bait., Lahm.), v. n. and a. [in-ludo].
Neutr., to play at or with any thing, to sport with, amuse one's self with (syn. colludo; cf. ludificor).
In gen. (very rare): illudo chartis,amuse myself with writing,: ima videbatur talis illudere palla,.—
In partic., pregn.
To make sport or game of, to jest, mock, or jeer at, to ridicule (class.).
With dat.: ut ne plane videaris hujus miseri fortunis et horum virorum talium dignitati illudere,: ut semper gaudes illudere rebus Humanis!: illudere capto,: discrimini publico,: inlusit Neroni fortuna,; cf. fin.—
In aliquem or aliquo: ego te pro istis factis ulciscar, ut ne impune in nos illuseris,; cf.: quae cum dixisset in Albucium illudens,: adeon' videmur vobis esse idonei, In quibus sic illudatis?.—
Absol.: illuseras heri inter scyphos, quod dixeram controversiam esse, etc.,. —
To sport or fool away a thing, i. e. to destroy or waste in sport; in mal. part., to violate, abuse (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
With dat.: cui (frondi) Silvestres uri assidue capraeque sequaces Illudunt,: pecuniae illudere,: C. Caesar etiam matri ejus illusit,: pueritiae Britannici,: feminarum illustrium capitibus,.—
Absol.: tum variae illudant pestes,.—
Act. (in all the meanings of I.).
In gen., to play at or with any thing (poet. and very rare): illusas auro vestes,i. e. lightly interwoven, (dub. al. inclusas); imitated by ; cf. the periphrase: illusa pictae vestis inania, Prud. στεφ. 14, 104.—
In partic., pregn.
To scoff or mock at, to make a laughing-stock of, to ridicule (so most freq.): satis superbe illuditis me,: ut is, qui illusus sit plus vidisse videatur. Quid autem turpius quam illudi?: miseros,: illusi ac destituti,: facetiis illusus,: pergisne eam, Laeli, artem illudere, in qua primum excello ipse?: artes,: ipsa praecepta (rhetorum),: illud nimium acumen (opp. admirari ingenium),: voces Neronis, quoties caneret,: verbis virtutem superbis,

.—

To destroy, ruin, violate, abuse (very rare): vitam filiae,: illusique pedes (i. e. crapulā) vitiosum ferre recusant Corpus, ruined, i. e. staggering, : corpus alicujus,.

illĭcĭo (inl-), lexi, lectum, 3 (
inf. perf. sync. illexe, Att. ap. ; Fragm. Trag. v. 205 Rib.; ), v. a.
in-lacio
, to allure, entice, attract, seduce, inveigle, decoy (most freq. in a bad sense; allicere oftenest in a good sense; cf.: invito, prolecto, inesco; mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; perh. only once in Cic.; not in Cæs.): qui non sat habuit conjugem illexe in stuprum, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 137 Rib.): is me ad illam illexit,: homines mente alienatos ad se (hyaena),: aliquem in fraudem,; ; : quos ad bellum spes rapinarum illexerat,: aliquem ad proditionem,: illectus praemio,: Gallorum fraude illectus,; : quin etiam illud par in utroque nostrum, quod ab eisdem illecti sumus,misled, led astray,: cavere, ne illiciaris,: invexisse in Galliam vinum, inliciendae gentis causa,: inlicite lucro mercatorem, ut, etc.,: quietos Inlicere, ut cuperent vitam mutare priorem,; so with ut, : inescandae illiciendaeque multitudinis causa,: pars dialectica utilis saepe illiciendo, implicando,.—Poet.: saltus, i. e. to surround with nets, Naev. ap. dub. (R conject.: sublimen alios in saltus inlicite). —In a good sense: ut populus illiciatur ad magistratus conspectum,be summoned, Müll.

la:verb:illucesco.html:
illūcesco or illūcisco (inl-), luxi, 3,
v. inch. n. and a. [in-lucesco].
Neutr., of the day or of the sun, to grow light, begin to shine, to break, dawn (most freq. in the tempp. perff.).
Lit.
Illucescet ille aliquando dies, cum tu, etc., : qui (dies) ut illuxit, mortui sunt reperti,: ne hic tibi dies inluxit lucrificabilis,; cf.: pro di immortales, quis hic illuxit dies? ap. ; : dies (alicui),; ; id. Ac. 2, 22, 69; : ea nocte, cui illuxit dies caedis, on which arose the day, etc., : cum tertio die sol illuxisset,: cum illucescerent elementa mundi,.—
Impers.: illuxit, it was light, day had dawned (very rare; not in Cic.; perh. not in Cæs.; for in B. C. 1, 23, 1, luxit is the better reading; v. Oud. ad loc.): ubi illuxit,; ; .—
Trop.: cum populo Romano vox et auctoritas consulis repente in tantis tenebris illuxerit,: clarissimum deinde Homeri illuxit ingenium,. —Impers.: apud quem si illuxerit, non universa pretia in patrimonium tuum processisse,shall be made clear, apparent,.—
Act., to shine upon, give light to (Plautin.): (nox) ut mortales illucescas luce clara et candida,: scelestiorem nullum alterum,.

,

Lit. (class.; in sing. and plur.; a favorite word of Cic.; cf.: invitatio, invitamentum).
With gen. (subj. or obj.): quae tanta in ullo homine juventutis illecebra fuit, quanta in illo?: maxima est illecebra peccandi impunitatis spes,: voluptas est illecebra turpitudinis,: fallax illecebra admirationum,: quaestionis,.—In plur.: habet etiam amoenitas ipsa vel sumptuosas vel desidiosas illecebras multas cupiditatum,: voluptatis,; : vitiorum (with lenocinia cupiditatum),: corruptelarum,.—
Absol.: munditia illecebra animo est amantūm,: ad quam illecebiam cum commoveretur nemo, etc., .—In plur.: suis te oportet illecebris ipsa virtus trahat ad verum decus,; : jocum tentavit, eo quod Illecebris erat et grata novitate morandus Spectator,.—
Transf., concr.

A plant, called also andrachne agria, ; .

la:adj:illiberalis.html:
illībĕrālis (inl-), e, adj.
in-liberalis
,
unworthy of a freeman, ignoble, ungenerous, sordid, mean, disobliging (class.; mostly of things): illiberales et sordidi quaestus mercenariorum omnium, quorum operae, non quorum artes emuntur,: labor,: facinus,: duplex omnino est jocandi genus, unum illiberale, petulans, flagitiosum, obscenum: alterum elegans, urbanum, ingeniosum, facetum,: res ad cognoscendum non illiberalis,: mens,: cibus (raphanus),: servom haud illiberalem praebes te,: non te in me illiberalem putabit,disobliging,.—

in-lino
, to put on by smearing or spreading, to smear, spread, or lay on (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: oculis collyria,: papavera madefacta teneris genis,: psyllion fronti,: anisum recens phreneticis,: solani folia contrita et illita,: aurum vestibus illitum,: aurum tecto,: aurum marmori,: faces taedamque et malleolos stuppae inlitos pice parari jubet,.—Poet.: quod si bruma nives Albanis illinet agris,spreads,: quodcumque semel chartis illeverit,has written,.—
Transf.
Aliquid aliqua re, to besmear, bedaub, anoint with any thing: ventrem alicui fimo,; : adustas gingivas melle,: texta Nesseo veneno,: pocula ceris,: faces taedamque et malleolos pice,: faces galbano,: navem bitumine ac sulphure,: porticum Medis,to paint,: tela dolis, et saep.—
Trop.: venustatis, non fuco illitus, sed sanguine diffusus color,daubed over with paint,: donum inimicorum veneno illitum,: vita illita maculā,.
